key_terms: A transactional managed table that uses write IDs, delta directories and compaction to support insert, update and delete.
The identifier Hive assigns to each transactional write so readers can determine which deltas are visible.
The Hive 4 integration that lets Hive create and query Iceberg tables through Iceberg's snapshot commit protocol.
Whether a given engine can correctly read a table's transaction protocol, file layout and delete representation.

worked_examples.title: Declare an Iceberg table through Hive
worked_examples.code:
CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ds60.orders_iceberg (id INT, region STRING, amount INT)
STORED BY ICEBERG
LOCATION 'file:///warehouse/orders_iceberg';

INSERT INTO ds60.orders_iceberg
VALUES
  (1, 'east', 4),
  (2, 'west', 9),
  (3, 'east', 7);
worked_examples.interpretation: From the prepared iceberg.hql, STORED BY ICEBERG means commits go through Iceberg metadata files and a pointer swap, not through Hive ACID delta directories. The Hive metastore stores only the table name and the current metadata_location property. After the insert, a metadata JSON and a snapshot should appear under the table location; if only data files appear, the Iceberg handler was not active and the result is not an Iceberg table.

worked_examples.title: Confirm a second reader sees the same snapshot
worked_examples.code:
table = catalog.load_table("ds60.orders_iceberg")
snapshot = table.current_snapshot()
print(snapshot.snapshot_id, table.metadata_location)
print(sorted(table.scan().to_arrow()["id"].to_pylist()))
worked_examples.interpretation: This PyIceberg fragment assumes a catalog object already configured against the same Hive metastore. A compatible second reader should print the same metadata_location that Hive stored and the IDs [1, 2, 3]. Matching rows with a different metadata location means the reader used another catalog or a stale pointer. Treat this as a prepared extension until both readers have actually run against the owned table.

evidence: Prepared actual Hive4.2.1/JDK21/PostgreSQL project; live SQL, independent Java Thrift, lifecycle, Iceberg and restore observations remain distinct acceptance gates.
